inventory.sourceFigureDescription: COLOR-CODED TABLE + TEXT BLOCKS, no raster (pdfimages: zero raster images; VLM-read in four passes, staging-pubh13/vlm-census.txt — VLM available this session): the running header (book page 265, SEC TION II, PUBLIC HEALTH SCIENCES, the banner '▶ PUBLIC HEALTH SCIENCES—EPIDEmIOLOGY AND BIOSTATISTICS' printing ONCE — running header only, no in-body ribbon on this page), the section header 'Statistical distribution' in dark teal-navy bold, row labels in teal semibold (Measures of central tendency / Measures of dispersion / Normal distribution / Nonnormal distributions, with the three Nonnormal sub-rows regular and indented; Null hypothesis / Alternative hypothesis / P value in the bottom block under its own 'Statistical hypothesis testing' header), body text in dark gray, dotted hairline row separators (no zebra striping), and RED BOLD printing in the hypothesis-testing rows — the subscript 0 of H0, the subscript 1 of H1, and the words 'zero' and 'one' (First Aid's own H0↔zero / H1↔at-least-one linkage, texttrace rgb 183,40,55). Rows: Mean = (sum of values)/(total number of values) — most affected by outliers (extreme values); Median = middle value of a list of data sorted from least to greatest — even number of values → the average of the middle two; Mode = most common value — least affected by outliers; Standard deviation = how much variability exists in a set of values, around the mean of these values; Standard error = an estimate of how much variability exists in a (theoretical) set of sample means around the true population mean; σ = SD; n = sample size; Variance = (SD)²; SE = σ/√n; SE ↓ as n ↑; Normal distribution — Gaussian, also called bell-shaped; mean = median = mode; for normal distribution, mean is the best measure of central tendency; for skewed data, median is a better measure of central tendency than mean; Bimodal distribution — suggests two different populations (metabolic polymorphism such as fast vs slow acetylators; age at onset of Hodgkin lymphoma; suicide rate by age); Positive skew — typically, mean > median > mode; asymmetry with longer tail on right; mean falls closer to tail; Negative skew — typically, mean < median < mode; asymmetry with longer tail on left; mean falls closer to tail; Null hypothesis — also called H0, zero difference between two groups or variables in the population; Alternative hypothesis — also called H1, at least one difference or association; P value — probability of obtaining test results at least as extreme as those observed in the sample, assuming H0 is correct; commonly accepted as 0.05 (<5% of such repeated tests would show results that extreme just by chance alone). Footer slug 'FAS1_2026_06-PubHealth.indd 265' + timestamp '12/16/25 12:46 PM'.

inventory.visualPurpose: The four stacked curve figures of the right-hand column (book 265): the normal bell with its graded σ bands and the 68%/95%/99.7% below-axis braces, the bimodal twin-peak curve, the positive-skew curve (markers Mode → Median → Mean), and the negative-skew curve (markers Mean → Median → Mode) — the page's visual comparison of distribution shapes and the anchor of every ordering question the exam asks from this page
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: PURE VECTOR ART, no raster (pdfimages: zero raster images; 159 path objects on the page, 102 in the figure column x≈417-537; geometry pinned by the four VLM passes + the PyMuPDF vector-geometry reconstruction + the pixel-visibility scan, staging-pubh13/vlm-census.txt — VLM available this session): FOUR distinct curve figures stacked vertically, each beside its table row. (1) NORMAL CURVE (beside 'Normal distribution'; x 425.9-532.3, baseline y 274.6, peak y 235.0, center x 478.6, σ≈10.5pt): a symmetric bell filled with six graded σ-band slices — center ±1σ light teal/mint, ±1σ-2σ pale lavender/periwinkle, ±2σ-3σ pale teal — with thin vertical teal dividing lines at each σ boundary; the σ tick labels –3σ…+3σ (en-dash minus signs) print INSIDE the curve at their band boundaries, cascading down the contour (–1σ/+1σ y 241.8 just under the peak; –2σ/+2σ y 255.7; –3σ/+3σ y 266.2 near the baseline); BELOW the solid dark navy horizontal axis, three nested horizontal curly braces with cusps pointing DOWN, each above its label, stacked under the curve's center: ±1σ brace (w 21pt) → '68%' (y 281.4), ±2σ brace (w 43pt) → '95%' (y 296.9), ±3σ brace (w 63pt) → '99.7%' (y 312.2) — 68% narrowest at top, 99.7% widest at bottom. (2) BIMODAL CURVE (beside 'Bimodal distribution'; humps at x≈451 and x≈494, saddle x≈476, baseline y 384.2): two rounded peaks of roughly equal height with a saddle between, plain light-teal fill, darker teal outline, thick dark navy baseline — NO σ ticks, NO percentage labels, NO Mode/Median/Mean markers. (3) POSITIVE SKEW (beside 'Positive skew'; peak left, long tail right, baseline y 444.4): three dashed teal vertical drop-lines (x 467.7/476.2/489.1) with markers printed left-to-right Mode (y 405.4, at the peak) → Median (y 408.6, just right of the peak) → Mean (y 422.7, down the tail slope). (4) NEGATIVE SKEW (beside 'Negative skew'; peak right, long tail left, baseline y 498.7): three dashed drop-lines (x 483.3/474.7/461.9) with markers printed left-to-right Mean (y 477.0, on the left tail) → Median (y 463.4, just left of the peak) → Mode (y 459.7, at the peak). Color furniture: light teal/aqua curve fills with darker teal outlines; σ tick labels small dark text; percentage labels dark; Mode/Median/Mean markers black/gray.
